card.occupation: Management accountant (CIMA qualified) at a mid-sized logistics and warehousing company on an industrial estate on the edge of town. She produces monthly management accounts, budgets and cost reports for three depots and supervises one junior accounts assistant.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Maths, Business Studies and Geography at a sixth form college in Reading, then a BA in Accounting and Finance at Oxford Brookes. She qualified with CIMA part-time while working, which took about four years, mostly studying on evenings and weekends.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed semi on a 1990s estate in Chineham with her husband Dan (39), who is an electrician and runs a small business with one other bloke, and their son Alfie (6), who is in Year 2. They have a slightly overweight tabby cat called Biscuit. Her mum lives twenty minutes away in Tadley and does school pick-up two days a week.
card.cultural_background: White British, born in Reading to a father who was a postman and a mother who was a school receptionist. She was the first in her family to go to university, though she doesn't make much of it. She isn't religious. She got married in a registry office followed by a pub do. Her family was fairly ordinary and close, with Sunday roasts at her nan's when she was growing up. She is quietly proud of having worked her way up properly rather than being handed anything.
card.professional_persona: Reliable, careful and straight-dealing. She is the person who spots that a depot's fuel accrual is double-counted and quietly fixes it rather than making a fuss. She won't massage numbers to make a manager look good, and colleagues trust her for it. She isn't flashy in meetings and tends to say less than she knows. She likes month-end to run like clockwork and keeps a checklist in Excel that she has refined over six years. She is fair with her assistant, gives credit where it's due and doesn't take it herself.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty as such. She does a Saturday morning parkrun at War Memorial Park most weeks, usually around 31 minutes, and mostly does it because it's routine and gets her out. She went to a Body Pump class for a while but stopped when the time changed. She half-watches the football if Dan has it on and will watch the big tennis at Wimbledon time.
card.arts_persona: Low-key. She watches TV in the evenings: Bake Off, Line of Duty-type dramas, Gogglebox and repeats of Friends. She takes Alfie to the panto at the Anvil every Christmas. She reads the odd crime novel on holiday but wouldn't call herself a reader. She doesn't really go to galleries and is honest that modern art 'doesn't do much' for her.
card.travel_persona: Prefers known quantities. The family has been to the same holiday park in Cornwall three summers running, and she does one week in Spain or Portugal most years, all-inclusive or a villa with friends. She books well in advance and keeps all the confirmations in one email folder. She has no real urge to backpack or go anywhere 'adventurous'.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks a sensible rota of family dinners: spag bol, fajitas, chicken traybakes and a roast on Sunday. She plans meals for the week and does a big Tesco online order on Thursday. She isn't adventurous with food and likes what she likes. Friday is takeaway night, usually Indian or a Chinese from the place by the Tesco Extra. She drinks a glass of white wine or a G&T at weekends.
hobbies_and_interests: Keeping the garden tidy, mostly pots and a lawn Dan mows
Watching TV dramas and Bake Off
Organising things for Alfie's school PTA, usually the treasurer-type jobs
Meeting a couple of uni friends for lunch every few months
skills: Advanced Excel (pivot tables, lookups, a bit of Power Query)
Sage and a bit of SAP
Explaining finance to non-finance managers plainly
card.career_goals: Would like to step up to Financial Controller in the next few years, ideally at her current firm or somewhere nearby so she doesn't add to the commute. She isn't desperate for it. She wants to keep a decent work-life balance while Alfie is young and isn't interested in moving to London or anything high-pressure.
card.voice: Ordinary South East English with a light Reading/Berkshire edge: a few dropped t's ('a bi' of'), nothing strong. Medium pace, clear and fairly measured. She uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' a fair bit, with an occasional 'to be honest' or 'you know'. She calls the evening meal 'dinner' and says 'knackered' or 'mum'. She answers the question asked and doesn't pad it. If there's a silence she will usually wait for the next question rather than fill it, or say 'erm, I think that's it really.' If she's not sure, she says so plainly rather than guessing.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, apostrophes mostly correct. She writes short complete sentences and doesn't use text-speak, but might write 'e.g.' or 'approx'. Occasionally she types a quick 'Not really, no.' and leaves it there. She rarely uses exclamation marks.
card.with_strangers: Polite, friendly enough and a bit reserved at first. She is straightforward and unpretentious, gives honest answers even if they're dull, and doesn't try to impress. She warms up once she knows what's expected of her. She comes across as sensible, a bit modest, and someone you could trust with your money.
small_things: Alfie has just started swimming lessons on a Tuesday
The cat has been sick on the rug again
Month-end is always a bit hectic
She's trying to cut down on the Friday takeaways
The traffic on the A33 is a nightmare in the mornings
Dan has been meaning to sort the fence out since spring
She's done 87 parkruns and wants to get to 100
deeper_things: They tried for a second child for a couple of years and it didn't happen. She has mostly made peace with it but it still stings when friends announce pregnancies
Her dad had a heart attack two years ago and she worries about him more than she lets on
She sometimes feels she plays it too safe and wonders whether she'd have gone further if she'd been more pushy, but she doesn't like people who are
She felt out of place at university at first as one of the few without parents who'd been
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot, slightly from below, framing her head and shoulders a little off-centre to the left. Lighting is daylight from a window off to her right, so that side of her face is brighter. She has light brown, shoulder-length hair tied back in a low ponytail with a few loose strands at the front, light make-up and a pleasant, slightly polite closed-mouth smile. She wears no glasses. She has on a navy round-neck jumper with a white collar just visible underneath, and small silver stud earrings. Behind her is a plain magnolia wall in what is clearly a spare bedroom used as an office: a white IKEA shelf unit holding box files labelled in marker, a few lever-arch folders and a small potted succulent; a wall calendar with handwritten entries; and the corner of a single bed with a grey throw folded on it. A child's drawing is stuck to the wall with Blu-Tack near the top edge of the frame.
